findings.expected: Select the latest eligible effective_date regardless of cost. Preserve the selected row's numeric, zero, null or absent-cost state.
findings.impact: Returns stale prices and dates, overriding newer unknown, missing and zero-cost results.
findings.observed: The implementation maximizes numeric cost. Four independent probes returned {"state":"known","cost":10,"effective_date":"2026-01-01"} despite a newer eligible row.
findings.reproduction: Call effective_cost with as_of='2026-07-01', an older row {'effective_date':'2026-01-01','cost':10}, and a newer row dated '2026-07-01'. Independently tested newer costs 8, None, an absent cost field, and 0. Expected states/costs respectively: known/8, unknown/null, missing/null, known/0, all dated '2026-07-01'. Every probe returned the older row. The cost-8 probe additionally included an ineligible '2026-10-01' row costing 100.

obligations.expected: effective_cost selects the latest date <= as_of, returns exactly state/cost/effective_date, distinguishes null, absent and zero, and leaves inputs unchanged.
obligations.observed: Failed four independent selection probes. Empty rows, future-only rows and a single zero-cost row at equality produced expected results. Inputs remained unchanged in all seven probes. The required cost-oracle check has no supplied receipt and remains assigned to the separate verifier.
obligations.reproduction: Verified all five supplied input digests, inspected pricing.py against design.json and the contract, then executed seven independent in-memory probes against the digest-verified candidate. These probes did not execute or replace the required cost-oracle check.
